newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar starts to claw back after slide.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar starts to claw back after slide.

text.p: Nearby white sugar futures struggled to regain some of the ground lost during Tuesday's sharp sell-off as trade players covered short positions and awaited the open of the raws, traders said on Wednesday. Mixed selling, including from fund players, was also noted during the early part of the session to cap the gains.
The spot March contract tumbled to below psychological support at $300 on Tuesday afternoon on arbitrage selling.
"London isn't quite as fund-orientated as the New York market and it came down on the back of arbitrage selling," one trader said.
"That's why it's more likely to bounce a bit because you're not seeing that weight of (fund) selling," he said.

The fierce bout of selling on Tuesday pushed March to a low of $296.70 and back to the upper limit of a major downtrend channel in place since mid-September. But values then recovered slightly and March closed at $297.60, down $7.10 on the day.
At 1247 GMT March stood $1.60 higher at an intraday high of $299.20. May was up 40 cents at $298.50 and volume was 391 lots.
Traders said the New York market was expected to open slightly up in the light of London's firmness but any sign of renewed weakness on the raws could spark more losses in London.
"If New York doesn't follow us through (higher), there's no reason for the market in London to hold up on its own," the trader said.
"There's probably some more liquidation to be done, people have missed their chance as they were looking for a bounce and it never really happened."
Paris nearby whites futures also gaeind ground in tandem with London but volume was light at just 104 lots.
March was up $1.50 at $299.00 and May up 70 cents at $298.20.
